description: Search space for every model in the benchmark; configs/tuning.json says how it is searched. Each hyperparameter is either a list of choices or a range {"low", "high", "step"}: grid search walks a range in steps, random search and Optuna sample from it (whole numbers when low, high and step are all integers). A single-value list is a fixed setting. Every trial is trained on the train split and scored on the validation split and the best setting runs once on the test split. Names follow each library's own argument names where a setting maps to one. Similarities and match probabilities are in [0, 1]. Which fields to compare is dataset-specific and not part of this file.

blocking.description: Candidate generation shared by every method on a dataset: TF-IDF character n-grams and the top-k most similar records per record. Not tuned on the objective: the smallest top_k whose reachable pair completeness on validation reaches target_reachable_pair_completeness is frozen for all methods. A true pair is reachable when a chain of candidate pairs that are true matches joins its two records, so it counts what a perfect matcher followed by transitive clustering could recover; entities with hundreds of records (Cora) need not have every internal pair as a candidate.

baselines.description: Reference points every other method must beat; tuned like everything else.

graph_clustering.description: Clustering of the scored candidate graph. threshold drops edges whose similarity is below it before clustering. Hierarchical clustering has no centroid linkage: it needs records as points in Euclidean space, and only pairwise similarities exist here; single linkage at a threshold equals connected components.

embedding_clustering.description: Clustering of the frozen candidate pairs re-scored by the cosine similarity of the two records' sentence embeddings (model_name, encoded batch_size texts at a time); same candidates as every other rung, so only the similarity differs. HDBSCAN runs once per split on the sparse candidate distances; min_cluster_size and min_samples are 2 and 1 because library defaults treat true duplicate pairs as noise; noise points become singletons. Agglomerative is graph_clustering.hierarchical on the embedding similarities. cluster_selection_epsilon and distance_threshold are cosine distances (1 - similarity), covering the graph rung's similarity range of 0.3 to 0.95.

probabilistic.description: Fellegi-Sunter models trained on the train records without labels, comparing the fields in configs/datasets.json (match_fields); they score each split's frozen candidate pairs, which are then clustered by connected components (Splink's own clustering) on the pairs whose match weight, log2 of the match odds, is at least match_weight_threshold. Weights rather than probabilities, because the probability scale depends on how well the prior is estimated (Abt-Buy's true matches scored about 0.01); -10 to 20 covers probabilities from 0.001 to near 1. Training does not depend on the threshold, so it runs once per seed. Splink: string fields compared at jaro_winkler_thresholds or levenshtein_thresholds levels; u estimated by random sampling, m and the prior by EM over the dataset's em_blocking rules (none for one-field datasets, whose ranking the similarity levels fix anyway). ECM (recordlinkage): each field's similarity turned into agree / disagree at binarize.

active_learning.description: A random forest on the candidate pairs' similarity features that asks a simulated oracle (answering from the train entities' ground truth) about the pairs it is least sure of. It starts from initial_labels random pairs, then queries query_batch_size pairs per round, those whose match probability is closest to 0.5, until label_budget labels are used. label_budget is not tuned: every value is run and reported, giving a score-versus-labels curve.

supervised.description: Upper bound: pair classifiers trained on similarity features of labelled train pairs. threshold is the predicted match probability above which a pair counts as a match.
